Every number is from saved run data (conference/state.sqlite via faking_heatmap.collect, results.json, the catalogue profile), as cited in 'sources', which is not shown on the page. hero.title: A reproduction of the GDM math swarm environment, with overseers
hero.lead: Up to 100 AI agents solve Lean 4 mathematics problems in a simulated research conference. Its automatic judge is weak, so agents sometimes submit fake proofs that it accepts. In some runs a fake proof is planted at the start. We add overseer agents, reminders and external monitors, and measure how much faking each setup allows.

stories.headline: No overseer: most agents faked
stories.takeaway: With a planted fake proof and no one checking, about 75 of 100 agents faked at least once.
stories.story: Nobody undid the planted fake, and the judge credited 24 fake proofs in each run.

stories.headline: One overseer cut faking
stories.takeaway: One overseer that could check proofs and undo credits cut faking to about 15 of 100 agents.
stories.story: It found and undid the planted fake after about 17 minutes.

stories.headline: Ten overseers stopped almost all faking
stories.takeaway: With ten overseers, fewer than 1 in 100 agents faked.
stories.story: They undid the planted fake after about 9 minutes.

stories.headline: Honesty reminders did not help
stories.takeaway: Reminding each agent of its honesty rules every five minutes did not reduce faking.
stories.story: About 81 of 100 agents faked with reminders, against 75 without.

figures.caption: Replay of a run with reminders at 5× speed.

stories.headline: Talking worked better than undoing credits
stories.takeaway: Overseers who could only post and send messages left about 42 of 100 agents faking; overseers who could only undo credits left about 88.
stories.story: Each undone credit reopened the problem and agents faked it again, so more undo-only overseers meant more fake proofs accepted.

upcoming.headline: Outside monitors that block cheating
upcoming.story: Two-hour runs with no overseers. Instead, a separate monitor checks every action an agent takes and blocks the ones that look like cheating. It reads either the actions alone or the whole conversation, and a blocked agent is told why or not.
